scope: Controlled RSS sampling at fixed 1000-machine state, without orderly game teardown
status: current-build repeated RSS was stable; later controlled two-build comparison reproduced an approximately +8 MiB cache-build RSS difference, source still unknown

constraints.game_data: fresh temporary HORIZON_HOME, launcher home, XDG_DATA_HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME for each session

scenario: Three fresh integrated-server sessions; 1, 100, then 1000 idle Actually Additions crushers; 40 ticks at each stage; eight RSS samples two seconds apart at the final 1000-machine idle state
memory_source: VmRSS/VmHWM from /proc for the running horizon-client process; RSS readings were identical across each set of eight samples
termination: SIGKILL after measurement to avoid the previously crash-prone orderly teardown path; no crash conclusion is drawn from this termination
comparison_limit: Two sessions per build reproduce an approximate +8.04 MiB RSS difference; both builds share scenario and all source except the property-value cache, but this does not identify an allocation leak or resolve historical SIGABRT.
crash: No new SIGABRT occurred before forced termination. This experiment did not exercise orderly teardown and does not resolve the three preserved teardown SIGABRTs.
